query: The Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy forms several primary non-eutectic phases during solidification and exhibits a complex, multistep crystallization sequence. Under rapid cooling, slower cooling, and subsequent reheating assessed by thermal analysis, what single intervention could increase amorphous retention and thermal stability while overcoming extensive primary crystallization? State one hypothesis containing the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted outcome relative to the alloy’s reported glass formation and crystallization behavior, the relevant cooling-rate and reheating boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing 2 at.% of P with B in the equiatomic Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy (yielding Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P18B2) will (i) suppress the nucleation of the observed primary non-eutectic phosphide phases during solidification and (ii) raise the first-crystallization onset temperature during reheating by ≥20 °C, thereby increasing amorphous retention and the supercooled-liquid region compared with the base alloy at the same cooling rate.
generation.material_initial_state: Arc-melted master alloy ingot of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20, rapidly re-melted before quenching.
generation.intervention: Micro-alloy 2 at.% B at the expense of P (Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P18B2). No other processing changes.
generation.conditions: Cooling: melt-spinning or copper-mould casting at 10³–10⁵ K s⁻¹. Reheating: DSC at 20 K min⁻¹ under high-purity Ar.
generation.structural_mediator: B promotes stronger, chemically frustrated metal–metalloid short-range order and increases packing density, reducing interfacial energy for competing phosphide nuclei while lowering atomic mobility in the supercooled liquid.
generation.mechanism:
1. Chemical frustration: B forms covalent-metallic bonds with Cr, Fe and Ni, destabilising the Cr–P and (Fe,Co)–P compounds that otherwise precipitate first.
2. Kinetic slowing: the small atomic radius of B suppresses long-range diffusion, raising the effective viscosity and delaying nucleation and growth.
3. Enthalpic stabilisation: the added B deepens the liquid-state eutectic, increasing reduced glass-transition temperature (Tg/Tl) and supercooled-liquid width ∆Tx.
generation.predicted_outcome:
Compared with the baseline alloy at identical cooling rates:
• X-ray diffraction of as-quenched ribbons shows a fully amorphous halo; volume fraction of crystalline phases falls from >30 % to <5 %.
• DSC reheating: first crystallisation onset (Tx1) shifts from ≈520 °C to ≥540 °C; the number of exothermic peaks is reduced.
• Critical casting thickness for fully glassy structure rises from <30 µm to ≥100 µm.
generation.baseline: Base alloy retains amorphous structure only in <30 µm ribbons at ≥10⁴ K s⁻¹; Tx1 ≈520 °C with three overlapping exotherms indicating multistep crystallisation.
generation.boundary: Effect expected for 0.5–3 at.% B substitution and cooling rates between 10² and 10⁵ K s⁻¹. Outside this B range or for cooling rates <10² K s⁻¹, primary crystallisation is predicted to re-emerge.
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative shifts (e.g., +20 °C in Tx1, four-fold increase in dc) are estimated; actual values may vary with impurity level and cooling uniformity. No prior data for this exact composition were available.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two melts: (A) baseline Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20, (B) modified Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P18B2. Produce melt-spun ribbons at 2 wheel speeds (30 m s⁻¹ ≈10⁵ K s⁻¹ and 15 m s⁻¹ ≈10⁴ K s⁻¹).
measurements: XRD for phase identification of as-spun ribbons
TEM selected-area diffraction for residual crystallinity
DSC at 20 K min⁻¹ to obtain Tg and Tx
Optical/SEM cross-sections to determine maximum fully-glassy thickness
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: Hypothesis is falsified if (i) Tx1 of alloy B is ≤ Tx1 of alloy A +10 °C, or (ii) amorphous volume fraction in alloy B does not exceed that of alloy A by at least 20 %, or (iii) maximum fully-glassy thickness of alloy B is ≤1.5 × that of alloy A under identical cooling conditions.
